en: Good morning, sir, thank you for giving me this opportunity.
tamil: காலை வணக்கம் சார், எனக்கு இந்த வாய்ப்பு கொடுத்ததுக்கு நன்றி.
context: Greeting the interview panel when you enter the room.
explain: A polite opening line. 'Thank you for giving me' shows respect and good manners.
usage: Say it with the panel at the start of an interview, right after you sit down.
leelaQ: How would you greet the panel at the start of an interview?
answer: I would say good morning and thank you for the opportunity.

en: Please tell us a little about yourself.
tamil: உங்களைப் பத்தி கொஞ்சம் சொல்லுங்க.
context: The interviewer starts the interview with the most common question.
explain: 'Tell us about yourself' is the usual first question. 'A little' means a short answer is enough.
usage: An interviewer says this to start the conversation and see how you speak.
leelaQ: Can you introduce yourself to me in two or three lines?
answer: I am Karthik from Madurai, and I am a computer science graduate.

en: I completed my engineering in Coimbatore in 2022.
tamil: நான் 2022-ல கோயம்புத்தூர்ல என் இன்ஜினியரிங் முடிச்சேன்.
context: Talking about your education in an interview.
explain: 'Completed' is past tense, used for a finished course. Use 'in' with a city and with a year.
usage: Use it when the interviewer asks about your studies and your college.
leelaQ: Where did you complete your studies, and in which year?
answer: I completed my degree in Trichy in 2021.

en: I am a quick learner and I enjoy working in a team.
tamil: நான் சீக்கிரமா கத்துக்குவேன், டீம்ல வேலை செய்யவும் எனக்குப் பிடிக்கும்.
context: Describing your good qualities to the interviewer.
explain: Two good qualities joined with 'and'. 'Quick learner' means someone who learns new things fast.
usage: Say it when you introduce yourself or when asked about your qualities.
leelaQ: What are two good qualities you have as a worker?
answer: I am hardworking, and I always help my teammates.

en: What do you think is your biggest strength?
tamil: உங்களோட மிகப் பெரிய பலம் என்னன்னு நினைக்கிறீங்க?
context: The interviewer asks about your main strength.
explain: A very common interview question. 'Do you think' inside the question keeps 'is' in normal order.
usage: Expect it in almost every interview, from freshers and experienced people alike.
leelaQ: Tell me, what is your biggest strength at work?
answer: My biggest strength is that I finish my work on time.

en: My biggest strength is that I stay calm under pressure.
tamil: என்னோட பெரிய பலம் என்னன்னா, அழுத்தத்துல நான் அமைதியா இருப்பேன்.
context: Answering the strength question in an interview.
explain: 'Is that I ...' joins the strength with a full sentence. 'Under pressure' means in a stressful time.
usage: A good answer for jobs with deadlines, such as support, sales or IT.
leelaQ: How do you feel when there is too much work and a short deadline?
answer: I stay calm and make a plan to finish everything step by step.

en: I can adjust to any shift the company needs.
tamil: கம்பெனிக்கு எந்த ஷிஃப்ட் தேவையோ அதுக்கு நான் அட்ஜஸ்ட் பண்ணிக்குவேன்.
context: Telling HR that you are flexible about timings.
explain: 'Adjust to' means to change yourself to suit something. 'Any' shows you are very flexible.
usage: Say it to HR when you want to show you are flexible and ready to work.
leelaQ: Are you flexible with your working hours?
answer: Yes, I can adjust to morning or evening hours.

en: I led a small team of four people in my last project.
tamil: என்னோட கடைசி ப்ராஜெக்ட்ல நான் நாலு பேர் கொண்ட சின்ன டீமை லீட் பண்ணினேன்.
context: Giving an example of your leadership skill.
explain: 'Led' is the past of 'lead'. 'Of four people' tells the size of the team.
usage: Use it when the interviewer asks for proof of leadership or teamwork.
leelaQ: Have you ever led a group at college or at work?
answer: Yes, I led my college team in a final year project.

en: I do not give up easily when a problem is difficult.
tamil: பிரச்சனை கஷ்டமா இருந்தா நான் சுலபமா விட்டுக் கொடுக்க மாட்டேன்.
context: Showing that you are determined during an interview.
explain: 'Give up' means to stop trying. 'Do not ... easily' shows you keep trying for a long time.
usage: A good line when asked how you face problems or failure at work.
leelaQ: What do you do when a task is very difficult?
answer: I try again and I ask my seniors if I need help.

en: My friend working here told me about this opening.
tamil: இங்க வேலை செய்யற என் ஃப்ரெண்ட் இந்த காலியிடத்தைப் பத்தி சொன்னாரு.
context: Answering how you came to know about the job.
explain: 'Working here' tells which friend. 'Opening' means a vacancy, a job that is free to apply.
usage: Use it when you came by a referral from a friend or a relative at the company.
leelaQ: Who told you about your current or last job?
answer: My cousin told me about it, and I applied the same day.

en: I have worked as a customer support executive for three years.
tamil: நான் மூணு வருஷமா கஸ்டமர் சப்போர்ட் எக்ஸிக்யூட்டிவா வேலை செஞ்சிருக்கேன்.
context: Explaining your work experience in an interview.
explain: Present perfect with 'for three years' shows experience that connects the past with now.
usage: Say it when the interviewer asks how much experience you have.
leelaQ: How many years of work experience do you have?
answer: I have two years of experience in sales.

en: Could you explain the role in a little more detail?
tamil: இந்த ரோலைப் பத்தி இன்னும் கொஞ்சம் விவரமா சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking the interviewer to describe the job.
explain: 'Could you ...?' is a polite request. Asking about the role shows that you are interested.
usage: Ask it politely when you want to know the exact work of the job.
leelaQ: What would you ask the interviewer about the job?
answer: I would ask what my daily work will be.

en: I am currently working at a software company in Chennai.
tamil: நான் இப்போ சென்னையில ஒரு சாஃப்ட்வேர் கம்பெனில வேலை செய்யறேன்.
context: Telling the interviewer where you work now.
explain: Present continuous with 'currently' shows something that is happening at this time.
usage: Use it when asked about your present job and place of work.
leelaQ: Where are you working at the moment?
answer: I am working in a small shop near my house.

en: Are you comfortable with a lot of travel?
tamil: நிறைய பயணம் செய்யறது உங்களுக்கு சௌகரியமா இருக்குமா?
context: HR asks about travel for a sales job.
explain: 'Comfortable with' means you feel fine about something. 'A lot of' is used for big amounts.
usage: Sales, field and audit jobs often have this question from HR.
leelaQ: Do you like travelling for work, or do you prefer staying in one place?
answer: I like travelling because I get to meet many new people.

en: Yes, I am ready to travel whenever the work needs it.
tamil: ஆமா, வேலைக்குத் தேவைப்படும்போதெல்லாம் பயணம் செய்ய நான் தயார்.
context: Telling HR you can travel for the job.
explain: 'Whenever' means every time that. 'Ready to' is followed by the base verb.
usage: Use it when the job needs field visits or outstation trips.
leelaQ: Are you ready to go on a work trip next week?
answer: Yes, I am ready, and I can pack in one day.

en: I will give my best effort from the very first day.
tamil: முதல் நாள்ல இருந்தே என்னோட முழு முயற்சியையும் போடுவேன்.
context: Promising hard work when the interviewer asks what you will do for the company.
explain: 'Will' shows a promise. 'Very' makes 'first day' stronger. 'Best effort' means the most you can do.
usage: A confident way to end an answer about what you will bring to the job.
leelaQ: What will you do in your first week at a new job?
answer: I will learn the work and help my team as much as I can.

en: Have you handled any difficult customers before?
tamil: இதுக்கு முன்னாடி கஷ்டமான கஸ்டமர்களை நீங்க சமாளிச்சிருக்கீங்களா?
context: The interviewer tests your customer handling skills.
explain: Present perfect with 'before' asks about experience in life up to now.
usage: Asked in support, retail and hotel interviews to check your patience.
leelaQ: How do you talk to a customer who is angry?
answer: I listen to him calmly and then I try to solve the problem.

en: Yes, I once calmed down an angry customer and solved his problem.
tamil: ஆமா, ஒரு தடவை கோபமா இருந்த கஸ்டமரை சமாதானப்படுத்தி அவரோட பிரச்சனையை தீர்த்து வச்சேன்.
context: Giving an example of handling a customer complaint.
explain: 'Once' means one time in the past. 'Calmed down' is a phrasal verb meaning made someone quiet.
usage: Use a short story like this when the interviewer asks for an example.
leelaQ: Can you tell me about a time you helped someone with a problem?
answer: Yes, I helped my neighbour fix his phone last week.

en: I am not afraid of hard work.
tamil: கடினமா உழைக்க எனக்குப் பயம் இல்லை.
context: Showing a strong attitude to the interviewer.
explain: 'Not afraid of' means you are brave about something. 'Hard work' means a lot of effort.
usage: Freshers use it to show they will work seriously even with little experience.
leelaQ: Do you like jobs that need a lot of hard work?
answer: Yes, I do, because hard work helps me learn faster.

en: My English is not perfect, but I am improving every day.
tamil: என்னோட இங்கிலீஷ் முழுசா சரியா இல்ல, ஆனா தினமும் முன்னேறிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Being honest about your English in an interview.
explain: 'But' joins a weak point with a good point. 'Am improving' shows steady progress.
usage: An honest and positive answer when the interviewer asks about your English.
leelaQ: How are you improving your English these days?
answer: I practise speaking for ten minutes every day.

en: In five years, I want to grow into a team leader role.
tamil: அஞ்சு வருஷத்துல ஒரு டீம் லீடர் பொசிஷனுக்கு வளரணும்னு ஆசைப்படறேன்.
context: Sharing your career goal with the interviewer.
explain: 'Grow into' means slowly become. 'Want to' is followed by the base verb.
usage: Use it to answer the future plans question with a clear and realistic goal.
leelaQ: What job position would you like to reach one day?
answer: I would like to become a manager after some years.

en: I enjoy solving problems, so this role suits me well.
tamil: எனக்கு பிரச்சனைகளை தீர்க்கறது பிடிக்கும், அதனால இந்த ரோல் எனக்குப் பொருத்தமா இருக்கும்.
context: Linking your interest with the job role.
explain: 'Enjoy' is followed by an -ing word. 'So' gives the result. 'Suits me' means is right for me.
usage: Say it when the interviewer asks why you are right for the job.
leelaQ: What kind of work do you enjoy doing most?
answer: I enjoy fixing technical problems and helping people.

en: Could you tell me more about the team I would work with?
tamil: நான் யாரோட டீம்ல வேலை செய்வேன்னு இன்னும் கொஞ்சம் சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking the interviewer about the team.
explain: 'Could you' is a polite way to ask. It shows you are interested in the job.
usage: Use it at the end of an interview to show interest in the role.
leelaQ: Who would you like to work with in your next job?
answer: I would like to work with friendly and helpful people.

en: I am not comfortable with night shifts because of my family.
tamil: குடும்பம் காரணமா எனக்கு நைட் ஷிஃப்ட் வசதியா இருக்காது.
context: Honestly telling HR about a limit.
explain: 'Not comfortable with' is a polite way to say no. Give a short reason.
usage: Use it with HR when you must be honest about timing limits.
leelaQ: Which work timing is best for you?
answer: Day time is best for me because I can be with my family.

en: I have been working as an accountant for four years.
tamil: நான் நாலு வருஷமா அக்கவுண்டன்டா வேலை செய்யறேன்.
context: Explaining your work experience.
explain: 'Have been working' with 'for' shows an activity that started in the past and continues now.
usage: Use it when the interviewer asks about your experience.
leelaQ: How long have you been doing your current work?
answer: I have been working in this job for three years.

en: I want this job because your company has a good name for training freshers.
tamil: ஃப்ரெஷர்ஸுக்கு நல்லா ட்ரெயினிங் குடுக்கறதுல உங்க கம்பெனிக்கு நல்ல பேரு இருக்கறதால இந்த வேலை வேணும்.
context: Explaining why you want the job as a fresher.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason. 'Has a good name for' means is known well for something.
usage: A freshers' answer to why they chose this company.
leelaQ: Why do you like the company you want to work for?
answer: I like it because it gives good training and growth.

en: I have read about your company, and I like the way you treat employees.
tamil: உங்க கம்பெனியைப் பத்தி படிச்சேன், நீங்க ஊழியர்களை நடத்தற விதம் எனக்குப் பிடிச்சிருக்கு.
context: Showing that you did your homework before the interview.
explain: 'Have read' shows you did it before now. 'The way you treat' means how you behave with people.
usage: It shows the interviewer that you prepared and that you respect the company.
leelaQ: What do you look for in a good company?
answer: I look for a company that respects its employees.

en: Why did you leave your previous job?
tamil: உங்க முந்தைய வேலையை ஏன் விட்டீங்க?
context: The interviewer asks about your last job.
explain: 'Did' + base verb for past questions. 'Previous' means the one before this.
usage: Experienced candidates always get this question, so answer it positively.
leelaQ: Why did you leave your last place of work or study?
answer: I left because I wanted to learn something new.

en: I left because I wanted more chances to learn new things.
tamil: புதுசா கத்துக்க இன்னும் நிறைய வாய்ப்பு வேணும்னு விட்டேன்.
context: Giving a positive reason for changing jobs.
explain: A positive reason without blaming the old company. 'Chances' here means opportunities.
usage: A safe and polite answer when asked why you changed your job.
leelaQ: What new thing do you want to learn this year?
answer: I want to learn how to use data tools at work.

en: I did not leave because of any problem with my manager.
tamil: என் மேனேஜரோட எந்த பிரச்சனையாலயும் நான் வேலையை விடல.
context: Clearing a doubt about why you changed jobs.
explain: 'Did not' + base verb is the past negative. 'Because of' is followed by a noun.
usage: Use it to show you left on good terms with your old company.
leelaQ: Did you have a good relationship with your last manager?
answer: Yes, he was kind, and I learned a lot from him.

en: What were your main duties in your last company?
tamil: உங்க கடைசி கம்பெனியில உங்களோட முக்கிய வேலைகள் என்ன?
context: The interviewer asks about your past responsibilities.
explain: 'Duties' means the tasks that are your responsibility. 'Were' goes with the plural 'duties'.
usage: Asked while checking your resume, to see what you actually did.
leelaQ: What were your daily tasks in your last job or course?
answer: I answered calls and updated the customer records.

en: I handled customer calls and prepared the daily sales report.
tamil: கஸ்டமர் கால்ஸை கையாண்டேன், தினசரி விற்பனை ரிப்போர்ட்டும் தயார் பண்ணினேன்.
context: Describing your work in the last company.
explain: Two past actions joined by 'and'. 'Handled' means dealt with, and 'prepared' means made ready.
usage: Use short action sentences like this to describe your past duties.
leelaQ: What reports or documents do you make at your work?
answer: I make a weekly report and send it to my manager.

en: I am looking for a job where I can grow along with the company.
tamil: கம்பெனியோட சேர்ந்து நானும் வளர முடியற ஒரு வேலையைத் தேடறேன்.
context: Telling the interviewer what kind of job you want.
explain: 'Looking for' means searching. 'Along with' means together with. It shows long term interest.
usage: Shows that you want a long career and not just a quick job.
leelaQ: What kind of job are you looking for?
answer: I am looking for a stable job with good learning chances.

en: Please have a look at my resume, sir.
tamil: என் ரெஸ்யூமை ஒரு தடவை பாருங்க சார்.
context: Handing your resume to the interviewer.
explain: 'Have a look at' means to see something. 'Please' and 'sir' make the request polite.
usage: Say it when you hand over your file to the panel in the interview room.
leelaQ: What do you carry with you when you go for an interview?
answer: I carry my resume, my certificates and a pen.

en: Do you have any experience with Excel?
tamil: உங்களுக்கு எக்செல்ல ஏதாவது அனுபவம் இருக்கா?
context: The interviewer checks your computer skills.
explain: 'Experience with' is followed by a tool or a skill. 'Any' is used in questions.
usage: Asked for office, accounts and data jobs.
leelaQ: Which computer programs can you use well?
answer: I can use Word and Excel quite well.

en: Yes, I use Excel every day to track orders and make charts.
tamil: ஆமா, ஆர்டர்களை டிராக் பண்ணவும் சார்ட் போடவும் நான் தினமும் எக்செல் பயன்படுத்தறேன்.
context: Describing your Excel skills with a real example.
explain: 'Every day' goes with the simple present for habits. 'To track' tells the purpose.
usage: Give real examples of how you use a tool, not only its name.
leelaQ: How often do you use a computer for your work?
answer: I use it every day for emails and reports.

en: Have you worked on any live projects?
tamil: நீங்க ஏதாவது லைவ் ப்ராஜெக்ட்ல வேலை செஞ்சிருக்கீங்களா?
context: The interviewer asks a fresher about practical work.
explain: A 'live project' is real work for a real client, not only a college assignment.
usage: Often asked in IT interviews to see if you have practical knowledge.
leelaQ: Have you done any practical project in your studies?
answer: Yes, I made a small billing app for a local shop.

en: I have done two live projects, and both were delivered on time.
tamil: ரெண்டு லைவ் ப்ராஜெக்ட் பண்ணிருக்கேன், ரெண்டுமே சரியான நேரத்துல குடுத்துட்டோம்.
context: Proving your work with results.
explain: 'On time' means not late. 'Were delivered' is passive and focuses on the project.
usage: Use numbers and results like this to make your answer more believable.
leelaQ: Do you finish your work on time most days?
answer: Yes, I plan my day so that I never miss a deadline.

en: I do not have much experience, but I learn very fast.
tamil: எனக்கு அதிக அனுபவம் இல்ல, ஆனா ரொம்ப வேகமா கத்துக்குவேன்.
context: Being honest as a fresher with a positive point.
explain: 'Much' is used with negatives. 'But' brings a good point after a weak point.
usage: A good answer when you are a fresher and the job needs experience.
leelaQ: How quickly do you learn new things?
answer: I learn quickly when I get a chance to practise.

en: When can you join us if we select you?
tamil: நாங்க உங்களை செலக்ட் பண்ணா எப்போ ஜாயின் பண்ண முடியும்?
context: HR asks about your joining date.
explain: This uses 'if' for a possible case. 'Select' is present tense, and 'can' asks about ability.
usage: HR asks this at the end to know your notice period.
leelaQ: How soon can you start a new job?
answer: I can start within two weeks.

en: I can join within fifteen days of getting the offer letter.
tamil: ஆஃபர் லெட்டர் கிடைச்சு பதினைஞ்சு நாளுக்குள்ள நான் ஜாயின் பண்ணுவேன்.
context: Telling HR your joining time.
explain: 'Within' means not later than. 'Of getting' is followed by an -ing word.
usage: Use it with HR when they ask about your notice period.
leelaQ: How long is your notice period at your present job?
answer: My notice period is one month.

en: Could you tell me what the next steps are?
tamil: அடுத்து என்ன நடக்கும்னு சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking about the hiring process at the end.
explain: After 'tell me', the word order is normal: 'what the steps are'. It is a polite indirect question.
usage: Ask it at the end of the interview to show interest in the process.
leelaQ: What do you usually ask at the end of an interview?
answer: I ask when I can expect to hear the result.

en: I am doing my notice period now, and it ends next month.
tamil: இப்போ நோட்டீஸ் பீரியட்ல இருக்கேன், அது அடுத்த மாசம் முடியுது.
context: Explaining your present job status to the HR person.
explain: 'Notice period' is the time you work after you resign. 'Ends' uses present for a fixed time.
usage: Say it when HR asks if you are free to join now.
leelaQ: Are you free to change jobs now or do you have to wait?
answer: I have to wait for one more month.

en: What did you like most about your last job?
tamil: உங்க கடைசி வேலையில உங்களுக்கு மிகவும் பிடிச்சது என்ன?
context: The interviewer asks about the best part of your old job.
explain: 'Most' shows the highest level. The answer should be positive and about work, not about money.
usage: It is a friendly question to know what motivates you.
leelaQ: What do you like best about your present work or studies?
answer: I like the people and the things I learn every day.

en: I liked the team the most, because everyone helped each other.
tamil: டீம் தான் எனக்கு ரொம்பப் பிடிச்சது, ஏன்னா எல்லாரும் ஒருத்தருக்கொருத்தர் உதவி செஞ்சாங்க.
context: Answering what you liked in your old job.
explain: 'Each other' is used when two or more people do the same thing to one another.
usage: A positive answer that shows you value teamwork.
leelaQ: Who is the most helpful person at your work or college?
answer: My friend Ravi is very helpful because he explains everything.

en: I have always wanted to work in the banking sector.
tamil: எப்பவுமே பேங்கிங் துறையில வேலை செய்யணும்னு எனக்கு ஆசை.
context: Showing your interest in a bank job.
explain: 'Have always wanted' shows a wish that started in the past and still continues.
usage: Say it when the interviewer asks why you chose this field.
leelaQ: Which field or industry do you want to work in?
answer: I want to work in the IT field.

en: Could I get a few minutes to think about that question?
tamil: அந்தக் கேள்வியைப் பத்தி யோசிக்க கொஞ்ச நேரம் கிடைக்குமா?
context: Asking for time when a question is difficult.
explain: 'Could I ...?' is a polite way to ask for permission. It is fine to take a moment to think.
usage: Use it politely instead of staying silent when you need time to answer.
leelaQ: What do you do when you do not know the answer to a question?
answer: I take a short pause and then try to answer calmly.

en: Please call me if you need any more documents.
tamil: உங்களுக்கு இன்னும் ஏதாவது டாக்குமெண்ட்ஸ் வேணும்னா எனக்கு போன் பண்ணுங்க.
context: Talking to HR after submitting your file.
explain: 'Please' makes the sentence polite. 'If you need' gives the condition.
usage: Use it with HR when you submit your certificates or resume.
leelaQ: What documents do you carry to an interview?
answer: I carry my resume, certificates and an ID card.

en: I will join immediately if you select me.
tamil: நீங்க என்னை செலக்ட் பண்ணா நான் உடனே சேர்ந்துடுவேன்.
context: Telling the interviewer you can start soon.
explain: 'Will' shows a promise. 'If' gives the condition for that promise.
usage: Use it when the interviewer asks how soon you can start.
leelaQ: When can you start a new job?
answer: I can start next week after I give notice.

en: What are the working hours here?
tamil: இங்க வேலை நேரம் என்ன?
context: Asking about the office timing.
explain: This is a simple, useful question about the job details.
usage: Use it with HR to ask about timings before accepting an offer.
leelaQ: What working hours do you like?
answer: I like to work from nine to six.

en: What salary are you expecting from this job?
tamil: இந்த வேலைக்கு எவ்வளவு சம்பளம் எதிர்பார்க்கறீங்க?
context: HR asks about your expected salary.
explain: 'Expecting' means thinking something will happen. This question is common near the end of the interview.
usage: HR asks this when the interview goes well and they discuss an offer.
leelaQ: What salary would you like in your next job?
answer: I would like a fair salary based on my skills.

en: I am expecting a package that matches my skills and experience.
tamil: என்னோட திறமைக்கும் அனுபவத்துக்கும் பொருந்தற மாதிரி ஒரு சம்பளம் எதிர்பார்க்கறேன்.
context: Answering the salary question politely.
explain: 'Package' means the full salary offer. 'Matches' means is equal to or suitable for.
usage: A safe and polite answer when you do not want to say a number first.
leelaQ: How do you decide what salary is fair for you?
answer: I compare it with my skills and the market rate.

en: My current salary is fifteen thousand a month.
tamil: என்னோட இப்போதைய சம்பளம் மாசத்துக்கு பதினைஞ்சாயிரம்.
context: Telling HR your present salary.
explain: 'Current' means at this time. 'A month' means for every month, like 'per month'.
usage: Say it when HR asks for your present pay before making an offer.
leelaQ: Do you get your salary monthly or weekly?
answer: I get my salary monthly on the first of every month.

en: Is the salary negotiable?
tamil: சம்பளத்தைப் பத்தி பேசிக்கலாமா?
context: Asking politely if the offered pay can change.
explain: 'Negotiable' means can be discussed and changed. A short, polite way to ask.
usage: Ask it politely with HR after you receive an offer.
leelaQ: Have you ever bargained for a better price or pay?
answer: Yes, I bargain when I buy things in the market.

en: Could you tell me the salary range for this position?
tamil: இந்த பொசிஷனுக்கு சம்பள வரம்பு எவ்வளவுன்னு சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking HR about the pay range.
explain: 'Range' means from the lowest to the highest amount. 'Could you tell me' is very polite.
usage: Use it with HR when you want to know the pay before giving your number.
leelaQ: What would you ask HR about the job offer?
answer: I would ask about the salary, leave and working hours.

en: I am open to discussion if the company has a fixed salary structure.
tamil: கம்பெனிக்கு ஒரு நிர்ணயிக்கப்பட்ட சம்பள அமைப்பு இருந்தா, நான் பேசத் தயார்.
context: Showing that you are flexible about salary.
explain: 'Open to' means ready to accept. 'Fixed structure' means the company pays by set rules.
usage: Say it when you want to sound flexible and not demanding.
leelaQ: Are you flexible when others suggest a different plan?
answer: Yes, I am open to new ideas and suggestions.

en: Money is not my only reason for changing jobs.
tamil: வேலை மாத்தறதுக்கு பணம் மட்டும் எனக்குக் காரணம் இல்ல.
context: Explaining your reason for changing jobs.
explain: 'Not only' means there are also other reasons. It shows growth matters to you too.
usage: Use it when the interviewer thinks you are changing jobs only for salary.
leelaQ: Besides money, what else is important to you in a job?
answer: A good team and learning chances are also important to me.

en: What is your biggest weakness?
tamil: உங்களோட மிகப் பெரிய பலவீனம் என்ன?
context: The interviewer asks about your weak point.
explain: A tricky question. Give a small, real weakness and say how you are improving it.
usage: Almost every interview has it, so prepare an honest and safe answer.
leelaQ: What is one habit you want to change in yourself?
answer: I want to stop delaying small tasks.

en: Sometimes I take too much work, but I am learning to say no politely.
tamil: சில நேரம் நான் ரொம்ப வேலையை எடுத்துக்கறேன், ஆனா மரியாதையா வேண்டாம்னு சொல்லக் கத்துக்கறேன்.
context: Answering the weakness question honestly.
explain: 'Too much' means more than needed. The second half shows that you are improving.
usage: A good weakness answer, because it shows both honesty and effort.
leelaQ: Is it easy for you to say no to someone politely?
answer: No, it is not easy, but I am trying to learn.

en: I do not like leaving a task half finished.
tamil: ஒரு வேலையை பாதியில விடறது எனக்குப் பிடிக்காது.
context: Showing responsibility in an interview.
explain: 'Do not like' is followed by an -ing word. 'Half finished' means not fully done.
usage: Use it when asked about your work habits or discipline.
leelaQ: What do you do when you start a task and feel tired?
answer: I take a short break and then finish the task.

en: Will you be able to work on Saturdays?
tamil: சனிக்கிழமைகள்ல உங்களால வேலை செய்ய முடியுமா?
context: HR asks about weekend work.
explain: 'Will you be able to' asks about future ability or willingness. 'On Saturdays' means every Saturday.
usage: HR asks this when the job has a six day week.
leelaQ: Are you okay with working on weekends sometimes?
answer: Yes, I am okay if it is only sometimes.

en: Yes, I will work on Saturdays if there is an urgent deadline.
tamil: ஆமா, அவசரமான டெட்லைன் இருந்தா சனிக்கிழமைகள்லயும் வேலை செய்வேன்.
context: Agreeing to weekend work for urgent tasks.
explain: 'If' with present tense and 'will' in the other part shows a real possible condition.
usage: Say it to show that you are committed, while keeping the condition clear.
leelaQ: What would you do if you had an urgent deadline tomorrow?
answer: I would stay late today and finish all the work.

en: Please tell me about the working hours.
tamil: வேலை நேரத்தைப் பத்தி சொல்லுங்க.
context: Asking HR about office timings.
explain: 'Please' makes the imperative polite. 'Working hours' means the time you work each day.
usage: Ask it politely when HR gives you the offer or the job details.
leelaQ: What time does your day at work usually start and end?
answer: It starts at nine in the morning and ends at six.

en: Is there any training for new employees?
tamil: புதுசா சேர்றவங்களுக்கு ட்ரெயினிங் ஏதாவது இருக்கா?
context: Asking about training at the end of the interview.
explain: 'Is there any ...?' asks if something exists. It shows you want to learn and grow.
usage: A good question to ask when the interviewer says 'Do you have any questions?'
leelaQ: What training would help you do your job better?
answer: A short course on communication would help me a lot.

en: I will be happy to take any training that the company gives.
tamil: கம்பெனி குடுக்கற எந்த ட்ரெயினிங்கையும் நான் சந்தோஷமா எடுத்துக்குவேன்.
context: Showing that you want to learn.
explain: 'That the company gives' tells which training. 'Be happy to' shows a willing attitude.
usage: Use it when the interviewer talks about training or new skills.
leelaQ: Are you happy to learn new software if your job needs it?
answer: Yes, I am happy to learn anything new.

en: How do you handle stress at work?
tamil: வேலையில வர்ற ஸ்ட்ரெஸ்ஸை எப்படி சமாளிக்கறீங்க?
context: The interviewer asks how you deal with pressure.
explain: 'Handle' means deal with. The question asks about your habits, so use the simple present.
usage: Asked for busy jobs like support, sales and banking.
leelaQ: What do you do when you feel tired or stressed?
answer: I listen to music and take a short walk.

en: When I feel stress, I make a to-do list and finish one task at a time.
tamil: ஸ்ட்ரெஸ் வந்தா, ஒரு டூ-டூ லிஸ்ட் போட்டு ஒரு நேரத்துல ஒரு வேலையை முடிப்பேன்.
context: Describing how you handle pressure.
explain: 'When' with present tense shows a habit. 'One at a time' means not many together.
usage: A practical answer that shows you can plan your work.
leelaQ: Do you make a list of your tasks every day?
answer: Yes, I write my tasks in my notebook every morning.

en: Can you give an example of a time you worked under a tight deadline?
tamil: இறுக்கமான டெட்லைன்ல நீங்க வேலை செஞ்ச ஒரு சந்தர்ப்பத்தை உதாரணமா சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: The interviewer asks for a real work example.
explain: 'Tight deadline' means very little time to finish. This is a behaviour question.
usage: Interviewers ask this to see real proof, not just big words.
leelaQ: When did you last finish something at the last minute?
answer: I finished my college assignment one hour before the deadline.

en: Last month, I finished a report in one day because the client needed it urgently.
tamil: போன மாசம், கிளையண்ட்டுக்கு அவசரமா தேவைப்பட்டதால ஒரு ரிப்போர்ட்டை ஒரே நாள்ல முடிச்சேன்.
context: Giving a real example of working fast.
explain: Past tense tells a real story. 'Urgently' means very quickly because it is important.
usage: A short story with time and result makes your answer strong.
leelaQ: Can you tell me about a time you worked very fast?
answer: I once cooked dinner for ten guests in one hour.

en: I once made a mistake in an invoice, but I told my manager and fixed it quickly.
tamil: ஒரு தடவை இன்வாய்ஸ்ல தப்பு பண்ணிட்டேன், ஆனா மேனேஜர்கிட்ட சொல்லி சீக்கிரமா சரி பண்ணினேன்.
context: Answering a question about a mistake you made.
explain: The story shows honesty. 'Fixed' means corrected. Three past actions are joined by 'and' and 'but'.
usage: A good answer when asked about a failure or a mistake at work.
leelaQ: What do you do when you make a mistake at work?
answer: I accept it and I correct it as soon as possible.

en: I prefer working in a team, but I can also work alone.
tamil: டீம்ல வேலை செய்யறது எனக்குப் பிடிக்கும், ஆனா தனியாகவும் வேலை செய்வேன்.
context: Answering the working style question.
explain: 'Prefer' is followed by an -ing word. 'Also' adds a second skill after 'but'.
usage: A balanced answer that works for most jobs.
leelaQ: When do you work better, alone or in a group?
answer: I work better alone when I need to concentrate.

en: I have never been late to office without informing my manager.
tamil: மேனேஜருக்குச் சொல்லாம நான் ஆஃபீசுக்கு தாமதமா வந்ததே இல்ல.
context: Showing that you are punctual and responsible.
explain: 'Never' with present perfect means not even one time in your life. 'Without informing' shows you tell people.
usage: Use it when asked about discipline, attendance or punctuality.
leelaQ: Are you usually on time for work or classes?
answer: Yes, I always reach ten minutes early.

en: I left my last job because I wanted to learn new things.
tamil: புதுசா கத்துக்கணும்னு ஆசைப்பட்டதால என் பழைய வேலையை விட்டேன்.
context: Explaining why you left your last job.
explain: Give a positive reason. 'Because' connects the action and the reason.
usage: Use it when asked why you left your previous company.
leelaQ: Why do you want to change your job?
answer: I want to learn new skills and grow in my career.

en: I was nervous in the beginning, but now I feel better.
tamil: ஆரம்பத்துல பயமா இருந்துச்சு, ஆனா இப்ப நல்லா இருக்கு.
context: Relaxing during the interview.
explain: 'But' joins two different ideas. It shows a change from past to now.
usage: Use it with a friendly interviewer when you feel more relaxed.
leelaQ: How do you feel before an interview?
answer: I feel a little nervous, but I prepare well.

en: Are you looking for a full-time or a part-time job?
tamil: நீங்க ஃபுல் டைம் வேலை தேடறீங்களா, பார்ட் டைம் வேலை தேடறீங்களா?
context: Interviewer asks about job type.
explain: This question gives two choices with 'or'. Answer with one clear choice.
usage: An interviewer asks this to know the kind of job you want.
leelaQ: Do you want a full-time job or a part-time job?
answer: I want a full-time job because I need a stable income.

en: Could you please explain the leave policy?
tamil: லீவ் பாலிசியைப் பத்தி சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking HR about leave rules.
explain: 'Policy' means the rules of a company. 'Please' makes your request polite.
usage: Ask it with HR when you receive the offer and want to know the rules.
leelaQ: How many days of leave do you get in a year?
answer: I get twelve days of casual leave in a year.

en: My parents are supportive, so relocating to Bengaluru is not a problem.
tamil: என் பெற்றோர் ஆதரவா இருக்காங்க, அதனால பெங்களூருக்கு மாறறது பிரச்சனை இல்ல.
context: Telling HR you can move to another city.
explain: 'Relocating' means moving to live in a new place. 'So' gives the result of the first part.
usage: Say it when the job is in another city and HR asks about moving.
leelaQ: Would you move to another city for a good job?
answer: Yes, I would move if the job is really good.

en: Thank you for your time, I really enjoyed our conversation.
tamil: உங்க நேரத்துக்கு நன்றி, நம்ம உரையாடல் எனக்கு ரொம்பப் பிடிச்சிருந்தது.
context: Closing the interview politely.
explain: 'Thank you for your time' is the standard way to close. 'Enjoyed' is past because it is finished.
usage: Say it when the interview ends and you stand up to leave.
leelaQ: How do you end a meeting politely?
answer: I thank them for their time and say goodbye.

en: Yes, what does a typical day look like in this role?
tamil: ஆமா, இந்த ரோல்ல ஒரு சாதாரண நாள் எப்படி இருக்கும்?
context: Asking the interviewer about daily work.
explain: 'Typical' means usual and normal. 'Look like' asks for a description of something.
usage: A smart question that shows you are thinking about the actual work.
leelaQ: What does a typical day look like for you?
answer: I wake up early, go to work and come home by seven.

en: Could you please let me know the result by next week?
tamil: ரிசல்ட்டை அடுத்த வாரத்துக்குள்ள தெரியப்படுத்த முடியுமா?
context: Asking when you will hear the result.
explain: 'Let me know' means tell me. 'By next week' means not later than next week.
usage: Say it politely at the end when you want to know the next step.
leelaQ: How do you politely ask someone for an answer by a certain date?
answer: I say could you please let me know by Friday.

en: I would be very happy to join your team.
tamil: உங்க டீம்ல சேர நான் ரொம்ப சந்தோஷப்படுவேன்.
context: Showing enthusiasm at the end of the interview.
explain: 'Would be happy to' is a polite way to say what you want. It shows a strong interest.
usage: Say it at the end to show that you really want the job.
leelaQ: Would you be happy to work with new people?
answer: Yes, I would be happy to meet new people and learn from them.

en: I will wait for your call, sir.
tamil: உங்க கால்க்காக காத்திருக்கேன் சார்.
context: Saying goodbye after the interview.
explain: 'Will wait' is a simple future promise. 'Sir' shows respect to the interviewer.
usage: A polite closing line when the interviewer says they will inform you.
leelaQ: What do you say when you are waiting for someone's reply?
answer: I say I will wait for your reply.

en: Please keep my resume for any future openings.
tamil: எதிர்காலத்துல ஏதாவது காலியிடம் வந்தா என் ரெஸ்யூமை வச்சுக்கோங்க.
context: Asking the company to remember you if you are not selected.
explain: 'Future openings' means jobs that will come later. It is a polite, hopeful way to close.
usage: Say it if you are not selected now but still want the company to call you later.
leelaQ: What would you say if you did not get the job?
answer: I would thank them and ask them to keep my resume.

en: It was nice meeting you, and I hope to hear from you soon.
tamil: உங்களைச் சந்திச்சது மகிழ்ச்சி, சீக்கிரமே உங்ககிட்ட இருந்து நல்ல பதில் வரும்னு நம்பறேன்.
context: Saying goodbye to the interviewer.
explain: 'It was nice meeting you' is used when you part. 'Hear from you' means get a message from you.
usage: A warm and polite closing line when you shake hands and leave.
leelaQ: What do you say when you leave after meeting someone new?
answer: I say it was nice meeting you and wish them well.

en: Is there anything else you would like to know about me?
tamil: என்னைப் பத்தி வேற ஏதாவது தெரிஞ்சுக்க விரும்பறீங்களா?
context: Offering more information at the end of the interview.
explain: 'Would like to' is polite. It gives the interviewer one more chance to ask you something.
usage: Ask it at the end of the interview to show that you are open and confident.
leelaQ: What else would you like to share about yourself?
answer: I would like to share that I love learning new skills.

en: I would like to say that I am very serious about this job.
tamil: இந்த வேலையில நான் ரொம்ப சீரியஸா இருக்கேன்னு சொல்ல விரும்பறேன்.
context: Making a final point to the interviewer.
explain: 'I would like to say that' introduces an important point. 'Serious about' means really committed.
usage: A strong closing sentence when you want to make a final impression.
leelaQ: What are you serious about in your life right now?
answer: I am serious about my career and my health.

en: When will we hear back from you?
tamil: உங்ககிட்ட இருந்து எப்போ பதில் வரும்?
context: Asking about the result date.
explain: 'Hear back' means get a reply after a first contact. 'When will' asks about a future time.
usage: A natural question near the end of an interview or a call.
leelaQ: How long do you wait for a reply after you apply for a job?
answer: I usually wait for about one week.

en: We will call you within a week to share our decision.
tamil: எங்க முடிவைச் சொல்ல ஒரு வாரத்துக்குள்ள உங்களுக்கு கால் பண்ணுவோம்.
context: The interviewer tells you when you will hear the result.
explain: 'Within a week' means in less than seven days. 'To share' tells the purpose of the call.
usage: An interviewer says this at the end, and you should reply with thanks.
leelaQ: What do you do while you wait for an important phone call?
answer: I keep my phone nearby and I stay busy with other work.

en: Congratulations, you have been selected for the next round.
tamil: வாழ்த்துகள், நீங்க அடுத்த ரவுண்டுக்குத் தேர்வாகியிருக்கீங்க.
context: HR calls to give you good news.
explain: 'Have been selected' is passive. It focuses on you and not on who selected you.
usage: HR says this on a phone call or an email after your first interview.
leelaQ: How would you feel if HR called you with good news?
answer: I would feel very happy and I would thank them.

en: Please bring your original certificates when you come for the next round.
tamil: அடுத்த ரவுண்டுக்கு வரும்போது உங்க ஒரிஜினல் சர்டிஃபிகேட்டுகளைக் கொண்டு வாங்க.
context: HR explains what documents to bring.
explain: 'Original' means not a copy. 'When you come' uses present tense for a future time.
usage: HR says this when they invite you for verification or the next interview.
leelaQ: Which documents do you take with you to an interview?
answer: I take my certificates, my ID card and some photos.

en: Could you send me the details of the next round by email?
tamil: அடுத்த ரவுண்டோட விவரங்களை ஈமெயில்ல அனுப்ப முடியுமா?
context: Asking HR for the interview details in writing.
explain: 'By email' tells the way. 'Details' means the time, place and other information.
usage: Ask it politely on a phone call so you do not forget the time or address.
leelaQ: Why is it good to get details by email after a phone call?
answer: It is good because I can read it again later.

en: I have attached my certificates to the email.
tamil: என்னோட சர்டிஃபிகேட்டுகளை ஈமெயில்ல இணைச்சிருக்கேன்.
context: Telling HR that your documents are in the mail.
explain: 'Attached' means added to an email. Present perfect shows the action is done just now.
usage: Write it in an email to HR when you send your documents.
leelaQ: Do you often send documents by email?
answer: Yes, I send documents by email almost every week.

en: Where is the interview going to be held?
tamil: இன்டர்வியூ எங்க நடக்கப் போகுது?
context: Asking for the interview venue.
explain: 'Going to be held' is a passive future for a planned event. 'Held' means conducted or organised.
usage: Ask it on a call with HR so that you reach the right place.
leelaQ: How do you find a new place when you go there for the first time?
answer: I use a map on my phone and I ask people on the way.

en: Please do not worry, the interview is just a simple conversation.
tamil: கவலைப்படாதீங்க, இன்டர்வியூ ஒரு சாதாரண உரையாடல்தான்.
context: Comforting a nervous friend before an interview.
explain: 'Please do not' + base verb gives a polite negative instruction. It is gentle and kind.
usage: Say it to a friend or a junior who feels nervous before an interview.
leelaQ: What do you say to a friend who is very nervous?
answer: I tell my friend to stay calm and just be honest.

en: I was a little nervous in the beginning, but now I feel better.
tamil: ஆரம்பத்துல கொஞ்சம் பயந்தேன், ஆனா இப்போ நல்லா இருக்கு.
context: Telling the interviewer how you feel after starting.
explain: 'Was' and 'feel' show a change from the past to now. 'A little' means slightly.
usage: Use it honestly when the interviewer says you look nervous.
leelaQ: Do you feel nervous when you speak in front of people?
answer: Yes, a little, but I feel better after the first minute.

en: Did you bring a copy of your resume?
tamil: உங்க ரெஸ்யூம் காப்பி கொண்டு வந்தீங்களா?
context: The interviewer asks for a printed resume.
explain: 'Did you bring' is a past question. 'A copy' means a printed paper version.
usage: A receptionist or interviewer asks it when you arrive for the interview.
leelaQ: Do you keep copies of your important papers?
answer: Yes, I keep copies of all my papers in a file.

en: Yes, I have brought two copies in this file.
tamil: ஆமா, இந்த ஃபைல்ல ரெண்டு காப்பி கொண்டு வந்திருக்கேன்.
context: Giving the copies of your resume to the interviewer.
explain: 'Have brought' shows that you have them now. 'In this file' tells where they are.
usage: Say it as you hand over the papers to the panel.
leelaQ: What do you carry in your bag every day?
answer: I carry my laptop, my lunch box and a water bottle.

en: Sorry, could you repeat the question once more?
tamil: மன்னிச்சிடுங்க, கேள்வியை இன்னொரு தடவை சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking the interviewer to repeat a question.
explain: 'Could you repeat' is polite. 'Once more' means one more time. It is better than guessing.
usage: Use it when you did not hear or understand the question well.
leelaQ: What do you say when you did not hear someone properly?
answer: I say sorry, could you please say that again.

en: I am sorry, I did not understand the question clearly.
tamil: மன்னிக்கணும், கேள்வி எனக்கு தெளிவா புரியல.
context: Telling the interviewer that you are confused.
explain: 'Did not understand' is the past negative. 'Clearly' shows that the problem is clarity.
usage: Say it politely instead of giving a wrong answer.
leelaQ: What do you do when you do not understand something in a meeting?
answer: I ask politely and I take notes.

en: Thank you for your time, and I hope to hear from you soon.
tamil: உங்க நேரத்துக்கு நன்றி, சீக்கிரம் உங்ககிட்ட இருந்து பதில் வரும்னு நம்பறேன்.
context: Ending the interview politely.
explain: This is a polite closing line. 'Hope to hear from you' means you want a reply.
usage: Say it at the end of the interview while leaving the room.
leelaQ: How do you say goodbye politely after a meeting?
answer: I say thank you for your time and shake hands.
